findings.title: Python's hash() on str is randomized per process, so group assignment is not stable
findings.body: `hash(group_key)` uses per-process hash randomization (PYTHONHASHSEED). Within one process the mapping is consistent, so in-process ordering holds. But the 'consistent hashing' docstring is misleading, and the assignment changes on every restart or rebalance. Use a stable hash such as crc32 or md5 if per-queue behaviour must be reproducible.

findings.title: Worker uses queue.ShutDown, which exists only in Python 3.13+
findings.body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` were added in Python 3.13. On earlier versions, `except queue.ShutDown` raises AttributeError and `q.shutdown` fails. The shutdown path swallows the failure via `except Exception`, so workers blocked in `get()` never wake. Shutdown then waits out the join timeout and leaves daemon threads behind. Also, `break` inside the `except queue.ShutDown` around `result_processor` skips nothing useful but is misplaced.

findings.title: Commit happens from a background thread, and state is shared across partition assignments
findings.body: The Arroyo `commit` callable is invoked from a separate thread, but Arroyo strategies are expected to call commit from the main consumer thread. The FixedQueuePool and OffsetTracker are created once by the factory and shared across every `create_with_partitions` call. After a rebalance, stale offsets and `last_committed` from revoked partitions persist. Items still queued from the old strategy can later be committed for partitions no longer owned. Also, `close()` on the strategy shuts down the shared pool, so the next strategy created by the factory after a rebalance gets a dead pool with no workers.

findings.title: Unbounded queues give no backpressure; docstring claims otherwise
findings.body: The queues are unbounded and `submit` never blocks or raises `MessageRejected`. The consumer will keep polling Kafka while a slow worker backs up, so memory grows without limit. The class docstring's claim of 'natural backpressure' is false.

findings.title: get_committable_offsets scans a Python range over offsets
findings.body: The loop iterates `range(start, max_offset+1)` under a lock every second. If offsets have large gaps (compacted or filtered topics), this becomes a very long loop. A gap also stops commits permanently, since a missing offset is never in all_offsets. For example, a skipped or non-contiguous offset blocks all further commits for that partition.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its docstring
findings.body: The docstring says errors don't block offset commits, but the assertion is `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. The test passes when nothing is committed, which hides the intended behaviour. It also only waits 2s for a 1s commit loop, so it can pass vacuously.
